verses.1: And during the reign of Rehoboam, as his kingdom grew stronger, he abandoned the laws of Jehovah and all of Israel along with him.
verses.2: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak, king of Egypt, invaded Jerusalem. This happened because they had rebelled against God.
verses.3: In ten thousand chariots, and in sixty thousand soldiers; there’s no end to the number of people who came with him from Egypt. They were mighty warriors and brave men.
verses.4: And he gathered together the cities of the tribes that belonged to Judah. Then he went on to Jerusalem.
verses.5: And when the prophet heard this, he went to Rahab and the leaders of Judah. They had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak. The prophet said to them, “Thus says the LORD: You have abandoned me, and I too have abandoned you in the hands of Shishak.”
verses.6: And the officers of Israel and the king became obedient. They said, “Righteous is the LORD!”
verses.7: And in His creation, it was revealed that Jehovah’s words would be fulfilled upon Shemaiah. He was told, “Do not defeat them; instead, give them a chance to live. Do not allow my anger to be unleashed in Jerusalem by Shishak.”
verses.8: For they will become his servants, and they will know how to serve Me and the kings of the nations.
verses.9: And Shishak, king of Egypt, came up against Jerusalem. He took away all the treasures of the Temple and those of the royal palace. He also took away all the gold objects that Solomon had made.
verses.10: And King Rehoboam made iron bars around them. He also assigned guards to watch over the door of the king’s palace.
verses.11: And when the king entered the Temple of God, the cherubim stood up and carried him back to the place where the cherubim were.
verses.12: And in his repentance, he left us. Even Jehovah did not destroy him for all his sins. And even in Judah, there were good things.
verses.13: King Rehoboam became stronger in Jerusalem. He ruled for forty-one years. He was king over Jerusalem, the city that Jehovah had chosen to place His name there, among all the tribes of Israel. His mother’s name was Naama the Maiden.
verses.14: And he did evil, because his heart was not prepared to obey Jehovah.
verses.15: And the words of Rehobam, both the earlier and later ones, are not written in the words of Shmaiah, the prophet, nor by him as a prophet. They were also not recorded during the wars between Rehobam and Yaravam over all those days.
verses.16: And Rehuel lay down with his fathers. He was buried in the city of David. Abiya, his son, ruled over him.
